script.title: Valuation of Unsold Stock on Consignment
script.caption_hook: Unsold goods in the consignee's godown still carry expenses. Here's how much.

lines.say: Unsold goods lying in the consignee's godown still carry expenses?
Yes! Unsold goods are valued at cost plus their share of non-recurring expenses incurred to bring them to the godown.
One-time costs up to the godown: freight, cartage, unloading. Rent and selling costs stay out.
Okay. Can we see a simple example?
1,000 units cost ₹1,00,000. Freight is ₹6,000, cartage and unloading ₹4,000. Expenses total ₹10,000.
So only the 200 unsold units' share of expenses goes in?
Yes, just their share. Take units unsold times cost plus expenses, over units sent.

board.title: Closing stock
board.sub: U unsold, Q sent, C cost, E expenses

lines.say: And if goods were sent at invoice price?
Take loaded invoice value plus expenses. Then create Stock Reserve for the loading on unsold goods.
How do I remember what goes in?
Till the door, not the floor. Stock carries its share of one-time expenses.

check_notes: Writer: Example: 1,000 units sent at cost ₹1,00,000; expenses ₹6,000 freight + ₹4,000 cartage/unloading = ₹10,000; 200 unsold gives ₹22,000 (₹20,000 + ₹2,000). Octroi replaced by cartage/unloading per feedback. Line 8 now answers "Yes" to the boy's question. Word count about 170 before the follow line.

Checker: Line 6/7 (example data): the example never says how many units were sold or remain unsold. The figure of 200 unsold units first appears in the student's question in Line 7, and the teacher simply confirms it. Correct version: state it in Line 6, for example '1,000 units sent costing ₹1,00,000; 800 sold, 200 remain unsold at the consignee's godown.' The ₹22,000 then follows only from data given in the example.

Checker: Line 8 board (formula): the key 'C cost, E expenses' doesn't say whether C and E are per-unit or total figures. The formula U × (C + E) / Q only works with totals. Correct key: 'C = total cost of goods sent, E = total non-recurring expenses, U = units unsold, Q = units sent.'

Checker: Line 7 (wording): 'only the 200 unsold units' share of expenses goes in' sounds as if only expenses are taken. The unsold units also carry their share of the cost. Better: 'So the 200 unsold units carry their share of cost and expenses?'
